title: Perseverance now holds the record for driving on another world, mostly steering itself
body: On 11 October 2026, its 2,006th Martian day, NASA's Perseverance rover made a 91.31 m drive that took its odometer to **45.22 km**, past the 45.16 km Opportunity drove between 2004 and 2018, the record for any vehicle on another world. Opportunity needed almost 15 years; Perseverance, about five and a half. It mostly steers itself. Commands take [3 to 22 minutes](https://science.nasa.gov/blog/speaking-percys-language-how-to-talk-so-perseverance-will-listen/) to reach Mars, so planners on Earth choose waypoints, and the rover's AutoNav photographs the ground while rolling, builds a 3D map of hazards and plots a path between them. More than 90% of its driving was done that way, against about 5% for the first autonav on Spirit and Opportunity, and it can cover up to 412 m in a single sol.

slides.question: Opportunity took almost 15 years to drive its record 45.16 km on Mars. How long did Perseverance take to pass it?
slides.explanation: About five and a half years, by NASA's count. It passed the record on 11 October 2026, its 2,006th sol on Mars.

slides.alt: Animation of Mars at dusk: an odometer rolls past Opportunity's 45.16 km to 45.22 km, and bars compare drives on Mars and the Moon. Then a top-down hazard map: the rover sees nearby rocks, plots a path to a waypoint and re-plans as it rolls. 20 points against 600,000; 5% against over 90%.

slides.prompt: Drive the rover to the waypoint. How far ahead must its self-driving AutoNav look to take the shortest route rather than a detour?
slides.takeaway: About 70 m. Looking 10 m ahead, it drives into the dead end and backs out: 341 m instead of 239. Without AutoNav it stops at the first rock and waits for Earth. A simplified map, but the same idea.

slides.heading: Farthest drives on other worlds
slides.note: NASA/JPL, October 2026. Curiosity and Perseverance are still driving.

slides.heading: Thinking while driving
slides.text: Perseverance can't be steered live from Earth. Its AutoNav takes pictures of the ground as it rolls, turns them into a 3D map of hazards and plots its course between waypoints chosen by the planners. Sojourner, in 1997, judged the path ahead from 20 measurement points; Perseverance processes 600,000 with every look.

slides.question: What do the planners on Earth give Perseverance for an AutoNav drive?
slides.explanation: They choose waypoints; the rover maps the hazards from its own pictures and plots the route between them. More than 90% of its 45 km was driven that way.

source.label: NASA/JPL: NASA's Perseverance Sets Off-World Record for Total Distance Driven (12 October 2026)
